icons.name: epoch-counter
icons.heading: Epoch counter
icons.description: A training pass completes and the counter registers it. Light: the two cycle arrows run one lap, each taking the other's place, overshoot a little and settle; as the lap lands the counter ticks, swelling and settling. Strong: the arrows wind back, run two laps with a stop between, and the counter ticks on each, the second harder. The tally never changes shape; the arrows end exactly where they started.

icons.name: loss-curve
icons.heading: Loss curve
icons.description: Training lowers the loss. Light: the latest loss point drops ten units in one move and stops dead, the trace bending down with it, while a faint copy of the old point stays behind for a moment and fades, showing how far it fell. Strong: two training steps: the point drops most of the way, pauses, then drops the rest; the old point lingers longer. The loss is data and never overshoots; the axes never move.

icons.name: gradient-step
icons.heading: Gradient step
icons.description: The parameter takes one step downhill. Light: the gradient vector thrusts along its direction and springs back, and the parameter block hops down one stair, landing on the next tread with a hit and a small rebound; then it is carried back up in one quick straight glide and set down on the top tread. Strong: the vector winds back and thrusts harder, and the block hops down two stairs, landing on each, before a quick glide carries it home while the vector ducks back out of its way. The stairs never move.

Strong: the bar climbs, stalls just under the benchmark, then breaks through to its score; the rule reaches across at the crossing and holds a beat before drawing back. The score never overshoots; the baseline never moves.

icons.name: convergence
icons.heading: Convergence
icons.description: The error closes and the run locks onto its target. Light: the upper and lower trajectories bend in toward the target in one move and stop dead in the narrow band; as they arrive the target ring takes the hit, swelling and settling. Strong: two training steps: the trajectories close most of the error and pause, then close the rest; the target answers each arrival, the last time harder with a two-swing settle. The starting observations stay fixed and the error never overshoots.
